newsitem.title: USA: Ground controllers flex shuttle robot arm.
newsitem.headline: Ground controllers flex shuttle robot arm.

text.p: NASA ground controllers tried their hand on Wednesday at operating a Japanese-made robot arm aboard the space shuttle Discovery.

The 5-foot (1.6 metre) long mechanical arm, intended for use on the proposed International Space Station, was tested by the shuttle crew before the controls were handed over to operators on the ground for the first time.

Discovery's astronauts used the arm to unbolt a box, move it about and put it back in place. Ground controllers were restricted to more basic movements, flexing the arm's shoulder, elbow and wrist joints.

The exercises were frequently stalled by computer and communications glitches and controllers were considering an extra work-out for the arm on Friday to complete the tests, mission control spokesman Ed Campion said.
The $100 million device was developed by the Japanese space agency to tend to experiments and equipment mounted to the exterior of a space station laboratory module.
A free-flying satellite, trailing Discovery by about 45 miles, continued a nine-day health check on the Earth's protective ozone layer.
Scientists said the satellite's study of the upper atmosphere was being complemented by measurements from small ground-fired rocket and weather balloons.
The German-built satellite is to be retrieved by the shuttle on Saturday. Discovery is to end its 11-day research flight on Monday.
